author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we develop largesample inference techniques for conditional exponential family models which are particularly suited for analyzing complex nonlinear timeseries data The framework we propose generalizes existing methods by accommodating a broad class of distributions facilitating a wide range of applications in timeseries analysis We establish asymptotic properties of the maximum likelihood estimators MLEs under varying conditions including scenarios with dependent observations typical in timeseries contexts The derived inference methods are shown to possess desirable properties such as consistency and asymptotic normality enabling robust estimation and hypothesis testing We illustrate the practical applicability of our results through simulations and realworld examples including nonlinear autoregressive models and conditional heteroskedasticity models Our findings underscore the utility of conditional exponential families in capturing the intricacies of nonlinear dependencies providing statisticians with powerful tools for model specification and inference in timeseries analysis

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: We consider a multivariate linear model with autocorrelated errors The mean vector of the process is assumed to be linear in the timetrend parameter beta and the withingroup variation parameter gamma The leastsquares estimators of beta and gamma and the related estimators of the autoregressive parameter theta and the error covariance matrix SIGMA are derived and their asymptotic distributions are obtained Large sample tests of H gamma and H beta are derived and the limit distributions of the restricted leastsquares estimators betaH and gammaH are obtained under H and H respectively

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Title Godambe Estimating Functions and Asymptotic Optimal InferenceAbstract In this paper we explore the theory of Godambe estimating functions which provide a unified framework for deriving parameter estimates that possess desirable asymptotic properties We begin by reviewing the foundational concepts behind estimating functions and their role in statistical inference emphasizing Godambes contributions to the development of efficient estimators We then extend existing results to establish conditions under which Godambe estimating functions yield asymptotically optimal estimators in a wide class of statistical models Our findings include new derivations of asymptotic variance and bias properties as well as applications to generalized estimating equations and semiparametric models We also illustrate the practical utility of Godambe estimating functions through simulation studies and realworld datasets demonstrating their robustness and efficiency compared to traditional estimation methods The implications of our results for hypothesis testing and model selection are discussed providing a comprehensive understanding of how Godambes approach can enhance statistical inference in practice This work contributes to the theoretical advancement of estimating function methodologies and highlights their relevance in contemporary statistical research

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: This article is concerned with explosive AR processes generated by conditionally heteroscedastic errors Conditional least squares as well as generalized least squares estimation for autoregressive parameter are discussed and relevant limiting distributions are expressed as products of certain random variables These results can be viewed as generalizations of classical results obtained for the standard explosive ARl model with iid errors cf Fuller WA Introduction to Statistical Time Series second ed Wiley New York Chapter The model under consideration accommodates diverse conditionally heteroscedastic processes including Engle Autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity with estimates of the variance of UK inflation Econometrica s ARCH thresholdARCH and betaARCH processes Based on residuals least squares estimation for parameters appearing in the conditional variance is also discussed and is illustrated for various ARCH type processes C Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: The asymptotic validity of the bootstrap for a test of criticality in a first order autoregressive AR process is established To circumvent the asymptotic invalidity of the standard bootstrap least squares estimator for the unstable case a sequential bootstrap procedure for the estimation of the parameter beta in the AR model Xt betaXt epsilont is studied The asymptotic validity of the sequential boostrap estimator is established for all textbackslashbetatextbackslash lessthanorequalto

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Parameter estimation based on the differences of two positive exponential family random variables is studied Waiting time data adjusted for idle times when necessary are used for estimating the parameters in GIGI queues The sampling plan presented uses incomplete information on the differences between service and interarrival times rather than full information on service and interarrival times A variation of the EM algorithm is proposed to derive parameter estimates Specific examples are discussed and the performances of the maximum likelihood and the corresponding estimates obtained by the EM algorithm are compared via simulations Related applications to inventory insurance and lifetesting models are briefly considered C Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Limit distributions both under the null and a sequence of alternative hypotheses are derived for the likelihood ratio and related statistics for testing the homogeneity of several autoregressive processes These results are extended to mixed autoregressive and moving average processes

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: In a previous paper Basawa efficient conditional tests were discussed for mixture experiments involving dependent observations The present paper is devoted to a study of the performance in large samples of a conditional maximum likelihood estimator and of a confidence limit for a parameter in a model specified by a mixture of a twoparameter exponential family The conditional estimator proposed in the paper is free from the mixing distribution and is efficient for all reasonable mixing distributions

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Godambe introduced a class of optimum estimating functions which can be regarded as a generalization of quasilikelihood score functions The optimality established by Godambe within a certain class is for estimating functions and it is based on finite samples The question that arises naturally is what if any asymptotic optimality properties do the estimators and tests based on optimum estimating functions possess In this paper we establish via presenting a convolution theorem asymptotic optimality of estimators and tests obtained from Godambe optimum estimating functions It is noted that we do not require the knowledge of the likelihood function C Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Critical random coefficient ARl processes are investigated where the random coefficient is binary taking values and Asymptotic behavior of least squares estimator for the mean of the random coefficient is discussed Ordinary least squares estimator is shown to be consistent Weighted least squares estimator turns out to be asymptotically normally distributed This enables us to present a unified limit result for the weighted least squares estimator valid for the stationary explosive and critical cases Also a test of criticality is discussed c Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Bifurcating autoregressive processes are used to model each line of descent in a binary tree as a standard ARp process allowing for correlations between nodes which share the same parent Limit distributions of the leastsquares estimators of the model parameters for a pthorder bifurcating autoregressive process BARp are derived An application to bifurcating integervalued autoregression is given A Poisson bifurcating model is introduced c Elsevier BV All rights

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Let Yt t be a stationary ergodic Markov process taking values on the real line and such that the transition density function belongs to a conditional exponential family In this paper we establish the local asymptotic normality LAN of the loglikelihood ratio for this model The LAN property leads to asymptotically optimal estimators and tests for the model parameters The results are then applied to a class of nonlinear time series which includes viz the random coefficient exponential and the random coefficient threshold autoregressive models

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Asymptotic validity of the bootstrap is established for the least squares estimate of the parameter of an explosive firstorder autoregressive process It is noted that nonnormal limit distributions are obtained for both the traditional and the bootstrap estimates The theoretical bootstrap validity results are supported by appropriate simulation

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Bifurcating autoregressive processes are used to model each line of descent in a binary tree as a standard ARp process allowing for correlations between nodes which share the same parent Limit distributions of the leastsquares estimators of the model parameters for a pthorder bifurcating autoregressive process BARp are derived An application to bifurcating integervalued autoregression is given A Poisson bifurcating model is introduced c Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractExplosive autoregressive processes characterized by their tendency to diverge over time present unique challenges in statistical modeling and inference Traditional methods often struggle to accurately estimate parameters and forecast future values due to the volatile nature of these processes In this paper we introduce a bootstrapping approach tailored specifically for explosive autoregressive models Leveraging both resampling techniques and model diagnostics our method significantly improves the robustness of parameter estimates and enhances prediction intervals compared to conventional techniques We provide theoretical justification for our approach including consistency and asymptotic properties and illustrate its practical application through extensive Monte Carlo simulations Additionally we apply our methodology to realworld time series data exhibiting explosive behavior demonstrating its effectiveness in providing reliable forecasts and informative uncertainty quantification Our findings highlight the utility of bootstrapping in addressing the inherent complexities of explosive autoregressive models paving the way for more resilient analytical frameworks in time series econometrics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we develop a comprehensive framework for conducting largesample tests of homogeneity in timeseries models addressing a crucial aspect of model diagnostics and validation in econometrics and related fields We propose a series of statistical tests designed to assess the equality of parameters across different time periods or subsamples within a given time series drawing on modern asymptotic theory Our methodology incorporates both parametric and nonparametric approaches allowing for robust inference in the presence of various forms of dependence and heteroskedasticity commonly encountered in timeseries data We demonstrate the effectiveness of our tests through a series of simulation studies that reveal their superior performance in terms of size and power compared to existing methods Furthermore we apply our proposed tests to several realworld datasets to illustrate the practical applicability of our approach revealing significant insights into structural changes over time The results underscore the importance of accounting for homogeneity in timeseries analyses providing a valuable toolkit for researchers seeking to enhance the reliability of their econometric models Overall our work contributes to the growing literature on timeseries modeling by equipping practitioners with rigorous statistical tools for evaluating homogeneity across time

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the application of leastsquares estimation techniques to bifurcating autoregressive processes which are commonly observed in nonlinear dynamics and time series analysis Bifurcating autoregressive models capture the complexities and structural changes inherent in many realworld phenomena including economic indicators ecological data and climate patterns We develop a theoretical framework for estimating model parameters under the leastsquares criterion focusing on the implications of bifurcation points on the stability and predictability of the resulting time series Through simulation studies we evaluate the performance of our proposed estimation method comparing it to traditional autoregressive estimation techniques Additionally we provide empirical examples demonstrating the efficacy of leastsquares estimation in identifying bifurcating behavior in historical datasets Our findings suggest that this approach not only enhances parameter estimation accuracy but also improves the understanding of dynamic systems exhibiting bifurcations This work contributes to the growing field of nonlinear time series analysis by offering robust statistical tools for model fitting and forecasting in bifurcating autoregressive processes

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the statistical properties of unstable firstorder autoregressive AR processes which pose challenges for traditional inference methods due to their nonstationary nature We propose a novel bootstrap test of significance tailored for AR processes exhibiting instability providing a robust framework for hypothesis testing despite the presence of divergent behavior in the data Furthermore we introduce a sequential bootstrap estimation technique designed to accurately estimate model parameters accommodating the timevarying dynamics inherent in unstable processes We demonstrate the efficacy of our methods through extensive simulation studies which reveal improved performance over conventional methods in terms of bias reduction and precision in parameter estimates Our findings contribute valuable insights into the analysis of unstable time series offering practical solutions for statisticians and practitioners working with autoregressive models in realworld applications

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we investigate the challenges and methodologies of parameter estimation in stochastic models when only partial information about the system is available We focus on queueing systems and related models where incomplete data can arise from various sources such as unobserved customer arrivals or service times We propose a novel approach that integrates likelihoodbased methods with partial data scenarios allowing for more robust parameter estimation Our framework leverages advanced statistical techniques including the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm and Bayesian inference to incorporate prior knowledge and uncertainty into the parameter estimation process We demonstrate the effectiveness of our methodology through a series of simulations and realworld applications showcasing its applicability to diverse queueing configurations and service disciplines The results indicate that our approach not only improves parameter estimates but also provides a deeper understanding of system dynamics in the presence of incomplete information Ultimately this work contributes to the field of queueing theory by enhancing estimation techniques that are crucial for both theoretical exploration and practical implementations in industrial and serviceoriented contexts

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the efficiency of conditional maximumlikelihood estimators CMLEs for parameter estimation in the context of mixtures of exponential families Mixtures of exponential families are widely used in statistical modeling due to their flexibility in accommodating diverse data distributions We derive the asymptotic properties of the CMLEs including their bias and variance and assess their efficiency relative to other estimation methods Additionally we propose confidence limits based on the CMLEs and evaluate their performance using simulation studies Our findings illustrate that CMLEs achieve asymptotic normality and exhibit a significant reduction in variance compared to traditional maximumlikelihood estimators in certain mixture settings The proposed confidence limits demonstrate good coverage properties across various sample sizes and mixture configurations enhancing inferential capabilities This study contributes to the understanding of parameter estimation in complex models and provides practical guidance for applying CMLEs in realworld scenarios involving mixtures of exponential families

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper addresses the challenges of largesample inference in the context of a multivariate linear model characterized by autocorrelated errors Traditional approaches to parameter estimation and hypothesis testing may lead to biased results when autocorrelation is present as it violates the assumptions of independence and homoscedasticity typically required in regression analyses We develop a robust framework for deriving asymptotic distributions of estimators and test statistics under the specified linear structure with autocorrelated errors Our methodology employs eigenvalue decompositions and suitable transformations to achieve consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators We establish the asymptotic properties of the maximum likelihood estimators and propose a set of diagnostic tools to assess the adequacy of the model fitted to the data Extensive simulation studies illustrate the efficacy of our approach in finite samples revealing significant improvements over existing techniques that fail to account for error correlation Finally we apply our method to a realworld dataset demonstrating its practical implications and the necessity of considering autocorrelation in multivariate regression settings Our findings contribute to the field by offering a viable solution for researchers dealing with complex error structures in large datasets

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper explores the application of Generalized Least Squares GLS estimation in the context of explosive autoregressive processes of order one AR with conditionally heteroscedastic errors While explosive AR models are crucial in various fields such as finance and environmental science their estimation poses significant challenges due to nonstationarity and the presence of timevarying volatility We develop a robust framework for GLS estimation that accounts for the explosive behavior in time series data and the heteroscedasticity of the error terms Our approach incorporates a flexible specification of the variance structure allowing for the modeling of dynamic volatility patterns commonly observed in practice We derive the theoretical properties of the proposed estimator including consistency and asymptotic normality under suitable assumptions Additionally we provide simulation studies to illustrate the performance of the GLS estimator compared to traditional methods highlighting its advantages in terms of bias reduction and efficiency in finite samples Application of the methodology to empirical datasets demonstrates its effectiveness in capturing volatile behaviors inherent in explosive processes Overall our findings contribute to the statistical literature by offering a novel estimation technique applicable to a range of economic and financial time series characterized by explosive and heteroscedastic dynamics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the application of least squares estimation methods for critical random coefficient firstorder autoregressive processes AR Such models encapsulate a wide range of dynamic systems where the coefficients exhibit randomness leading to significant implications in fields such as economics finance and environmental science We begin by defining the structural properties and stability criteria of critical random coefficient AR processes focusing particularly on the conditions under which these models maintain stationarity We then develop the least squares estimation framework providing a comprehensive derivation of the estimators and exploring their asymptotic properties including consistency and efficiency Through simulation studies we assess the finitesample performance of the proposed estimators highlighting their robustness in various scenarios of coefficient variability and noise levels The paper concludes with practical guidelines for model selection and application in realworld data analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of least squares estimation in capturing the underlying dynamics of critical random coefficient processes These findings contribute to the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of autoregressive models with random coefficients facilitating more accurate predictions and insights into complex time series phenomena

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents an innovative approach to statistical inference for the extended bifurcating autoregressive model specifically tailored to analyze cell lineage data Cell lineage studies are critical for understanding developmental biology and disease progression where the tracking of individual cell histories is essential The traditional modeling frameworks often fall short in capturing the complex branching structures inherent in lineage data We extend the bifurcating autoregressive model to incorporate additional parameters that allow for the nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies observed in cell lineages Using a combination of simulation studies and realcase biological datasets we carefully evaluate the performance of our model in terms of parameter estimation prediction accuracy and model robustness We employ Bayesian inference techniques to derive posterior distributions of the model parameters and provide a thorough discussion on the implications of our findings in the context of lineage tracing experiments The proposed model not only enhances the statistical understanding of cell dynamics but also offers a robust tool for researchers in developmental biology and medical research Our results demonstrate that the extended bifurcating autoregressive model significantly outperforms conventional methods paving the way for more nuanced interpretations of cell lineage data

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: We consider the problem of testing that a subvector of a finite dimensional parameter is zero against that it satisfies some inequality constraints in a semiparametric model To our knowledge this problem has not been studied in the literature in a general context Huang Ann Statist developed maximum likelihood estimation in a class of semiparametric models and Choi et al Ann Statist developed efficient tests against unrestricted alternatives in a large class of semiparametric models which includes the adaptable ones In this paper we introduce local tests as a general approach to developing tests against inequality constraints and apply them in different semiparametric models In particular we apply our local tests to develop adaptive tests and efficient tests in the classes of semiparametric models studied by Huang and Choi et al thus extending their results to inequality constrained framework C Published by Elsevier Science BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Two methods of bootstrap viz standard and conditional are presented for estimating the transition probabilities of a finite state Markov chain Asymptotic validity of the bootstrap estimates are established for both methods An applica tion to a bootstrapped statistic for testing independence is briefly discussed together with some simulation results

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: This paper explores recursive prediction and likelihood evaluation techniques for periodic autoregressive movingaverage PARMA time series models The innovations algorithm is used to develop a simple recursive scheme for computing onestepahead predictors and their mean squared errors The asymptotic form of this recursion is explored The prediction results are then used to develop an efficient and exact PARMA likelihood evaluation algorithm for Gaussian series We then show how a multivariate autoregressive moving average ARMA likelihood can be evaluated by writing the multivariate ARMA model in PARMA form Explicit calculations for PARMA models and periodic autoregressions are included

text: This article introduces threshold GARCH processes to which BoxCox transformations are applied This class of processes includes nonlinear ARCH and GARCH models as special cases The model accommodates asymmetries in conditional variances through a threshold The stationary solution is explicitly obtained and moment structures are investigated C Elsevier BV

text: Limit distributions both under the null and a sequence of alternative hypotheses are derived for the likelihood ratio and related statistics for testing the homogeneity of several autoregressive processes These results are extended to mixed autoregressive and moving average processes

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Huggins Basawa proposed several extensions of the bifurcating autoregressive model used to model cell lineage trees These models overcame limitations in the original bifurcating autoregressive mode by allowing larger correlations between cousin cells and other cells in the same generation Huggins Basawa only considered maximum likelihood inference based on independent trees This paper examines the asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimators based on a single large tree

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: For the critical and subcritical GaltonWatson processes with immigration it is shown that if the data were collected according to an appropriate stopping rule the natural sequential estimator of the offspring mean m is asymptotically normally distributed for each fixed m isanelementof Furthermore the sequential estimator is shown to be asymptotically normally distributed uniformly over a class of offspring distributions with m isanelementof bounded variance and satisfying a mild condition These results are to be contrasted with the nonsequential approach where drastically different limit distributions are obtained for the two cases a m normal and b m nonnormal thus leading to a singularity problem at m The sequential approach proposed here avoids this singularity and unifies the two cases The proof of the uniformity result is based on a uniform version of the wellknown Anscombes theorem

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive framework for recursive prediction and likelihood evaluation in periodic Autoregressive Moving Average ARMA models which are widely used for time series forecasting exhibiting seasonal patterns We aim to enhance the computational efficiency of traditional ARMA techniques by providing a novel recursive algorithm that facilitates realtime prediction updates and maximizes the use of historical data Our approach integrates advanced statistical methodologies to evaluate the likelihood of periodic ARMA models offering a robust solution to the challenges of nonlinear and autocorrelated time series The proposed method is rigorously tested against various synthetic and realworld datasets demonstrating superior performance in terms of predictive accuracy and computational speed compared to standard estimation techniques Additionally we provide a detailed analysis of the implications of periodicity in time series data and its influence on model behavior The results underscore the importance of recursive methodologies in achieving reliable forecasting outcomes thereby contributing to the growing body of literature in statistical modeling and time series analysis Our findings suggest pathways for future research and practical applications in diverse fields such as economics environmental science and engineering

text: AbstractIn this paper we develop a comprehensive framework for conducting largesample tests of homogeneity in timeseries models addressing a crucial aspect of model diagnostics and validation in econometrics and related fields We propose a series of statistical tests designed to assess the equality of parameters across different time periods or subsamples within a given time series drawing on modern asymptotic theory Our methodology incorporates both parametric and nonparametric approaches allowing for robust inference in the presence of various forms of dependence and heteroskedasticity commonly encountered in timeseries data We demonstrate the effectiveness of our tests through a series of simulation studies that reveal their superior performance in terms of size and power compared to existing methods Furthermore we apply our proposed tests to several realworld datasets to illustrate the practical applicability of our approach revealing significant insights into structural changes over time The results underscore the importance of accounting for homogeneity in timeseries analyses providing a valuable toolkit for researchers seeking to enhance the reliability of their econometric models Overall our work contributes to the growing literature on timeseries modeling by equipping practitioners with rigorous statistical tools for evaluating homogeneity across time

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper introduces a novel class of firstorder observationdriven integervalued autoregressive processes INAR which extend traditional autoregressive frameworks by incorporating stochastic dependence structures suitable for count data We establish the theoretical foundations of our model demonstrating its capacity to capture overdispersion and autocorrelation commonly observed in count time series The model employs a flexible linking function that facilitates the connection between the latent processes and observed counts allowing for a rich representation of the underlying datagenerating mechanisms We provide a thorough statistical estimation procedure utilizing the method of moments alongside an expectationmaximization EM algorithm for parameter estimation Additionally we conduct extensive simulation studies to evaluate the performance of the proposed model in recovering true parameter values under various scenarios Realworld applications are presented illustrating the models efficacy in capturing the dynamics of count data such as daily incidence of infectious diseases and retail sales transactions Our findings suggest that the firstorder observationdriven INAR processes are a powerful tool for modeling integervalued time series offering insights into both theoretical and practical aspects of count data analysis

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper explores the application of Generalized Least Squares GLS estimation in the context of explosive autoregressive processes of order one AR with conditionally heteroscedastic errors While explosive AR models are crucial in various fields such as finance and environmental science their estimation poses significant challenges due to nonstationarity and the presence of timevarying volatility We develop a robust framework for GLS estimation that accounts for the explosive behavior in time series data and the heteroscedasticity of the error terms Our approach incorporates a flexible specification of the variance structure allowing for the modeling of dynamic volatility patterns commonly observed in practice We derive the theoretical properties of the proposed estimator including consistency and asymptotic normality under suitable assumptions Additionally we provide simulation studies to illustrate the performance of the GLS estimator compared to traditional methods highlighting its advantages in terms of bias reduction and efficiency in finite samples Application of the methodology to empirical datasets demonstrates its effectiveness in capturing volatile behaviors inherent in explosive processes Overall our findings contribute to the statistical literature by offering a novel estimation technique applicable to a range of economic and financial time series characterized by explosive and heteroscedastic dynamics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the application of least squares estimation methods for critical random coefficient firstorder autoregressive processes AR Such models encapsulate a wide range of dynamic systems where the coefficients exhibit randomness leading to significant implications in fields such as economics finance and environmental science We begin by defining the structural properties and stability criteria of critical random coefficient AR processes focusing particularly on the conditions under which these models maintain stationarity We then develop the least squares estimation framework providing a comprehensive derivation of the estimators and exploring their asymptotic properties including consistency and efficiency Through simulation studies we assess the finitesample performance of the proposed estimators highlighting their robustness in various scenarios of coefficient variability and noise levels The paper concludes with practical guidelines for model selection and application in realworld data analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of least squares estimation in capturing the underlying dynamics of critical random coefficient processes These findings contribute to the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of autoregressive models with random coefficients facilitating more accurate predictions and insights into complex time series phenomena

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce and analyze a novel class of firstorder random coefficient integervalued autoregressive processes denoted as RInteger AR models These models extend the traditional integervalued autoregressive framework by incorporating random coefficients allowing for greater flexibility in capturing the dynamic behavior of count data observed in realworld applications We develop the theoretical underpinnings of the RInteger AR processes including conditions for stationarity and ergodicity and derive the associated likelihood function for model estimation Additionally we present a comprehensive simulation study to evaluate the performance of estimation techniques and showcase the adaptability of our model to various count datasets Finally we illustrate the practical applicability of the RInteger AR model through case studies in epidemiology and finance demonstrating its efficacy in modeling and forecasting overdispersed count series The results suggest that accounting for random coefficient variability significantly enhances model fit and predictive accuracy in integervalued time series analysis

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore sequential estimation methodologies for branching processes with immigration a framework that reflects population dynamics wherein individuals reproduce and new individuals enter the population from an external source We introduce a comprehensive statistical model incorporating both branching processes and immigration considering the impact of various immigration rates on population growth and structure Our approach develops sequential estimation techniques aimed at efficiently estimating key parameters including the reproduction and immigration rates from observed population data We derive the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators and examine their performance through simulations demonstrating their consistency and efficiency under different initial conditions and immigration scenarios Furthermore we apply our methodology to realworld datasets to validate its applicability and utility in demographic studies The results highlight the advantages of sequential methods in terms of adaptability and realtime inference paving the way for improved population management strategies in ecology and conservation biology

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract This paper examines the efficacy of statistical tests for inequality constraints in the context of semiparametric models which blend parametric and nonparametric components to capture complex data patterns Traditional approaches to hypothesis testing often rely on strict parametric assumptions that may not hold in realworld applications We develop novel testing procedures that accommodate general inequality constraints while ensuring robustness against model misspecification Our methodology involves leveraging a combination of kernel estimation and resampling techniques to derive consistent test statistics and critical values under both the null and alternative hypotheses Through simulation studies and empirical applications we demonstrate the improved power and reliability of our tests compared to existing methods By providing a framework for addressing inequality constraints this work contributes to the broader literature on semiparametric estimation and inference offering practitioners a powerful tool for understanding relationships influenced by inequality in diverse fields such as economics social sciences and biostatistics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we investigate the stationarity and moment structure of BoxCox transformed Threshold GARCH ll processes The BoxCox transformation is utilized to stabilize variance and normalize the data providing a robust framework for capturing the inherent characteristics of financial time series that often exhibit volatility clustering The study begins with a comprehensive review of the theoretical foundations of Threshold GARCH models emphasizing their ability to account for asymmetries and nonlinearities in volatility dynamics We derive conditions under which the BoxCox transformed processes retain stationarity focusing on the effects of varying transformation parameters on the stationarity conditions and moment properties By employing advanced mathematical tools and numerical simulations we explore the implications of different thresholds and transformation parameters on the existence of secondorder moments Our results demonstrate that careful selection of the BoxCox transformation parameters can enhance the modeling accuracy for empirical data exhibiting nonconstant volatility Additionally we provide practical guidelines for practitioners on the implementation of these transformed models in econometric applications The findings contribute to the literature by extending the understanding of the interplay between transformation techniques and volatility modeling offering new avenues for both theoretical exploration and practical applications in financial econometrics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: A firstorder random coefficient integervalued autoregressive RCINAR model is introduced Ergodicity of the process is established Moments and autocovariance functions are obtained Conditional least squares and quasilikelihood estimators of the model parameters are derived and their asymptotic properties are established The performance of these estimators is compared with the maximum likelihood estimator via simulation c Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: A firstorder observationdriven integervalued autoregressive model is introduced Ergodicity of the process is established Conditional least squares and maximum likelihood estimators of the model parameters are derived The performances of these estimators are compared via simulation The models are applied to a real data set C Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper investigates the asymptotic properties of bootstrap methods applied to finite Markov chains While bootstrap techniques have garnered significant attention in the statistical literature for their ability to provide valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests their performance in the context of Markov chains remains underexplored We establish conditions under which bootstrap methods yield valid asymptotic inference for key parameters of interest in finite Markov models Our analysis employs a rigorous framework that combines the theory of empirical processes with martingale convergence principles We demonstrate that under certain regularity conditions the bootstrap distribution converges in distribution to the limiting distribution of the original estimator ensuring valid inference The theoretical results are supported by a series of simulation studies that illustrate the practical performance of the proposed bootstrap methods Additionally we present an application of our findings to a realworld dataset showcasing the relevance of our methods in empirical research This work not only contributes to the understanding of bootstrap methods in dependent structures but also paves the way for new applications in Markov chain analysis enhancing the toolkit available for statisticians dealing with sequential data

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Based on intermittent observations from several independent regression models with autocorrelated errors we derive tests of homogeneity and the maximum likelihood estimate of the common regression parameter The estimate for the regression parameter is based on aggregated data in the form of sample means at each time point The limit distributions of the test statistics and the estimate are considered

text: Finite mixtures of Markov processes with densities belonging to exponential families are introduced Quasilikelihood and maximum likelihood methods are used to estimate the parameters of the mixing distributions and of the component distributions The EM algorithm is used to compute the ML estimates Mixture of Autoregressive processes and of twostate Markov chains are discussed as specific examples Simulation results on the comparison of quasilikelihood and ML estimates are reported C Elsevier Science BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Models for Markov processes indexed by a branching process are presented The new class of models is referred to as the branching Markov process BMP The law of large numbers and a central limit theorem for the BMP are established Bifurcating autoregressive processes BAR are special cases of the general BMP model discussed in the paper Applications to parameter estimation are also presented C Elsevier Inc

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: The local asymptotic normality for a class of generalized random coefficient autoregressive processes is established This property implies the asymptotic optimality of the maximum likelihood estimator and the related test statistics The model includes standard random coefficient autoregressive processes Markovian bilinear models and random coefficient exponential autoregressive processes as special cases

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Robust analogues of the Wald and the Rao score statistics are presented for testing composite hypotheses in time series models involving dependent observations Asymptotic efficiency and empirical power comparisons using moderate size samples are given for firstorder autoregressive processes Our method of robustifying the estimating equation gives a simple and unified approach which is useful in a large class of problems including regression with dependent errors and autoregressive and moving average processes Largesample properties of the robust procedures are given for these processes

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: The least squares estimators of the regression and the autoregression parameters are obtained for a regression model with random coefficient autoregressive errors The limit distribution of the least squares estimators are obtained using a weighted central limit theorem for mdependent processes The proof of the weighted central limit theorem for mdependent processes is also given

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive analysis of parameter estimation in regression models characterized by random coefficient autoregressive RCA errors The incorporation of random coefficients and autoregressive structures in error terms allows for a more flexible modeling framework that captures unobserved heterogeneity and dynamic dependencies in the data We develop a twostep estimation approach that combines generalized method of moments GMM with simulation techniques to address the challenges of estimation under heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation common in time series data The asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators are derived illustrating consistency and asymptotic normality under specified conditions Through simulated examples and realworld applications we demonstrate the efficacy of our method in accurately estimating regression coefficients and autocorrelation parameters relative to existing methodologies Our findings underscore the importance of utilizing robust statistical techniques in capturing the complex dynamics of realworld data offering valuable insights for both theoretical developments and practical applications in econometrics and related fields

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Observationdriven state space models are presented for categorical time series as an alternative to the regression type models which are commonly used in the literature As an application to multicategorical time series we present a DNA data analysis and demonstrate the advantages of using state space models C Elsevier BV All rights

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper addresses the estimation challenges associated with mixtures of Markov processes a model framework commonly encountered in various fields such as finance biology and social sciences We propose a novel approach that combines maximum likelihood estimation with the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm tailored for the mixture model setting Our methodology accounts for the underlying complexities of the transition dynamics among multiple Markov processes allowing for the identification of distinct regimes within the observed data We derive theoretical properties of the estimators including consistency and asymptotic normality and provide conditions under which these properties hold To illustrate the practical applicability of our method we apply the proposed estimation technique to simulated datasets as well as to realworld case studies demonstrating its effectiveness in recovering the true underlying mixture structure Comparative analyses with standard estimation methods reveal significant improvements in estimation accuracy and computational efficiency The findings suggest that our approach not only enhances the understanding of mixed Markov processes but also offers valuable tools for researchers and practitioners facing similar estimation problems in their respective domains

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel framework for modeling categorical time series data using Observationdriven Generalized State Space Models OSSMS Traditional state space models often struggle with the complexities inherent in categorical data particularly regarding nonGaussian distributions and latent process dynamics Our approach introduces a flexible structure that integrates generalized linear models within the state space formulation allowing for more effective handling of varying distributional characteristics of categorical observations We establish the theoretical underpinnings of OSSMS and demonstrate their capacity for capturing dynamic relationships and transitions in categorical time series Utilizing a Bayesian estimation framework we implement Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods to infer model parameters ensuring robust inference for complex datasets We apply our model to several realworld examples showcasing its advantages over conventional approaches in terms of predictive performance and interpretability The proposed OSSMS framework offers a comprehensive solution for analysts and researchers seeking to deepen their understanding of categorical time series data and its underlying dynamics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the application of least squares estimation methods for critical random coefficient firstorder autoregressive processes AR Such models encapsulate a wide range of dynamic systems where the coefficients exhibit randomness leading to significant implications in fields such as economics finance and environmental science We begin by defining the structural properties and stability criteria of critical random coefficient AR processes focusing particularly on the conditions under which these models maintain stationarity We then develop the least squares estimation framework providing a comprehensive derivation of the estimators and exploring their asymptotic properties including consistency and efficiency Through simulation studies we assess the finitesample performance of the proposed estimators highlighting their robustness in various scenarios of coefficient variability and noise levels The paper concludes with practical guidelines for model selection and application in realworld data analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of least squares estimation in capturing the underlying dynamics of critical random coefficient processes These findings contribute to the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of autoregressive models with random coefficients facilitating more accurate predictions and insights into complex time series phenomena

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: A generalized random coefficient autoregressive GRCA process is introduced in which the random coefficients are permitted to be correlated with the error process The ordinary random coefficient autoregressive process the Markovian bilinear model and its generalization and the random coefficient exponential autoregressive process among others are seen to be special cases of the GRCA process Conditional least squares and weighted leastsquares estimators of the mean of the random coefficient vector are derived and their limit distributions are studied Estimators of the variancecovariance parameters are also discussed A simulation study is presented which shows that the weighted leastsquares estimator dominates the unweighted leastsquares estimator C Elsevier Science BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we introduce a framework for parameter estimation in Generalized Random Coefficient Autoregressive GRCA processes a class of time series models that extends traditional autoregressive structures by incorporating random coefficients The GRCA model accommodates a wide range of applications where the relationship between current and past values is influenced by unobserved random effects We propose a twostep estimation approach combining method of moments and maximum likelihood techniques which efficiently estimates both the autoregressive parameters and the distribution of the random coefficients We conduct a comprehensive simulation study to assess the performance of our estimation method under various scenarios of model specification and noise structures Our results indicate that the proposed method yields consistent and asymptotically normal estimates substantially outperforming existing methods in terms of bias and mean squared error particularly in finite sample sizes Additionally we apply the developed estimation procedure to the analysis of realworld economic and financial time series data demonstrating the models practical applicability and robustness This work contributes to the statistical literature by enhancing the toolkit for modeling dynamic processes and addressing the complexities arising from randomness in coefficient estimation

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we investigate the properties of largesample inference in regression models that exhibit autocorrelated errors Specific attention is given to understanding how autocorrelation impacts the estimation of parameters and the validity of standard inference techniques We utilize a robust statistical framework to derive asymptotic distributions for regression estimators under the assumption of autoregressive error structures Our findings reveal that conventional estimation methods when applied without adjustment for autocorrelation can lead to biased standard error estimates and unreliable hypothesis tests We propose a set of remedies including generalized least squares GLS and robust inference procedures to mitigate these issues Through extensive simulation studies we compare the performance of these methods against traditional ones demonstrating significant improvements in estimation accuracy and inferential validity in the presence of autocorrelated errors Our results provide a comprehensive guide for practitioners and researchers enabling more reliable statistical analysis in regression contexts where error correlation is an intrinsic feature of the data This work contributes to the literature by bridging gaps in understanding the implications of error structures and providing practical solutions for effective inference in empirical research

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract In this paper we propose a set of robust statistical tests designed to analyze timeseries data specifically focusing on firstorder autoregressive AR processes Traditional methods for testing the properties of timeseries data often rely on assumptions of normality and homoscedasticity which can lead to invalid conclusions in the presence of outliers or other deviations from these assumptions Our robust tests utilize a combination of bootstrapping techniques and robust estimation methods to provide more reliable results under a wider range of conditions We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through simulation studies that compare the performance of our robust tests with standard methodologies Furthermore we apply our robust tests to a realworld financial dataset revealing insightful patterns in the underlying dynamics of the time series Our findings suggest that the new tests not only improve the robustness of parameter estimation in AR models but also enhance the overall understanding of temporal relationships in complex datasets This work contributes to the statistical toolkit available for timeseries analysis and underscores the importance of robustness in empirical applications

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: A conditional limit theorem is derived for a certain class of stochastic processes whose distributions constitute a nonergodic family The limit theorem allows us to study the asymptotic behaviour under the conditional model of some standard statistical procedures by making use of results for ergodic families Explosive Gaussian autoregressive processes are studied in some detail Here the conditional process is shown to be a nonexplosive Gaussian autoregression bearing a simple relation to the original process Some optimality results under the conditional model are given for estimators and tests based on the unconditional likelihood

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract This paper investigates the properties of branching Markov processes which serve as fundamental models in various fields including population dynamics genetics and queuing theory We focus on both the theoretical framework and the asymptotic behavior of these processes as they evolve over time By employing advanced probabilistic techniques we derive several key results pertaining to extinction probabilities growth rates and limiting distributions Our analysis reveals critical thresholds that influence the longterm behavior of the process particularly in relation to branching mechanisms and environmental factors We also explore the connections between branching Markov processes and other stochastic models highlighting their applications in realworld scenarios The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how branching dynamics unfold under Markovian assumptions and can inform future research directions in stochastic processes Through a combination of rigorous mathematical derivations and simulation studies we provide a comprehensive overview of the asymptotic properties of these processes laying the groundwork for further exploration in both theoretical and applied contexts

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the statistical properties of unstable firstorder autoregressive AR processes which pose challenges for traditional inference methods due to their nonstationary nature We propose a novel bootstrap test of significance tailored for AR processes exhibiting instability providing a robust framework for hypothesis testing despite the presence of divergent behavior in the data Furthermore we introduce a sequential bootstrap estimation technique designed to accurately estimate model parameters accommodating the timevarying dynamics inherent in unstable processes We demonstrate the efficacy of our methods through extensive simulation studies which reveal improved performance over conventional methods in terms of bias reduction and precision in parameter estimates Our findings contribute valuable insights into the analysis of unstable time series offering practical solutions for statisticians and practitioners working with autoregressive models in realworld applications

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate asymptotic conditional inference methods for regular nonergodic models with a particular focus on autoregressive processes Nonergodicity poses unique challenges in statistical inference as standard asymptotic results may not hold We establish a theoretical framework for conditional inference that accommodates nonergodic behavior enabling the derivation of valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests in such contexts Our approach utilizes conditioning on suitable algebras to exploit the underlying structure of the data while maintaining robustness against the irregularity introduced by nonergodicity We illustrate our methodology through applications to autoregressive models where we demonstrate the impact of nonergodicity on parameter estimation and inference Simulation studies corroborate the effectiveness of our proposed conditional methods in providing accurate statistical inference across various settings The findings shed light on the subtleties of inference in nonergodic regimes and contribute to the broader understanding of statistical modeling for time series data

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract This paper explores the local asymptotic normality LAN of a class of generalized random coefficient autoregressive GRCAR processes which incorporate dynamic structural changes and heterogeneous dependency structures We establish conditions under which GRCAR processes exhibit LAN properties demonstrating that the posterior distribution of the parameters converges to a multivariate normal distribution in the context of increasing sample sizes Utilizing a combination of martingale convergence theorems and the asymptotic theory of functional limit theorems we derive explicit expressions for the asymptotic covariance matrices of the estimators Moreover we investigate the implications of these findings for estimation and inference in nonstationary time series highlighting the robustness of GRCAR processes in capturing complex temporal dynamics Simulations illustrate the practical utility of our theoretical results validating the LAN framework as a powerful tool for analyzing the asymptotic behavior of parameter estimators in contemporary econometric applications Our findings contribute to the broader literature on time series analysis enhancing the understanding of the statistical properties of GRCAR processes under local perturbations

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive analysis of parameter estimation in regression models characterized by random coefficient autoregressive RCA errors The incorporation of random coefficients and autoregressive structures in error terms allows for a more flexible modeling framework that captures unobserved heterogeneity and dynamic dependencies in the data We develop a twostep estimation approach that combines generalized method of moments GMM with simulation techniques to address the challenges of estimation under heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation common in time series data The asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators are derived illustrating consistency and asymptotic normality under specified conditions Through simulated examples and realworld applications we demonstrate the efficacy of our method in accurately estimating regression coefficients and autocorrelation parameters relative to existing methodologies Our findings underscore the importance of utilizing robust statistical techniques in capturing the complex dynamics of realworld data offering valuable insights for both theoretical developments and practical applications in econometrics and related fields

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: This paper studies techniques for fitting parsimonious periodic time series models to periodic data Large sample standard errors for the parameter estimates in a periodic autoregressive movingaverage time series model under parametric constraints are derived Likelihood ratio statistics for hypothesis testing are examined The techniques are applied in modeling daily temperatures at Griffin Georgia USA

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: This paper is concerned with efficiency in testing for the mean of the offspring distribution of a supercritical GaltonWatson process It is suggested that the maximum likelihood estimator is generally inefficient for this problem in the sense that asymptotically it is not an optimum discriminator between alternative values of the parameter Three competing tests are discussed and their efficiency compared via an example

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: The least squares estimators of the regression and the autoregression parameters are obtained for a regression model with random coefficient autoregressive errors The limit distribution of the least squares estimators are obtained using a weighted central limit theorem for mdependent processes The proof of the weighted central limit theorem for mdependent processes is also given

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Observationdriven state space models are presented for categorical time series as an alternative to the regression type models which are commonly used in the literature As an application to multicategorical time series we present a DNA data analysis and demonstrate the advantages of using state space models C Elsevier BV All rights

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Models for Markov processes indexed by a branching process are presented The new class of models is referred to as the branching Markov process BMP The law of large numbers and a central limit theorem for the BMP are established Bifurcating autoregressive processes BAR are special cases of the general BMP model discussed in the paper Applications to parameter estimation are also presented C Elsevier Inc

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Huggins Basawa proposed several extensions of the bifurcating autoregressive model used to model cell lineage trees These models overcame limitations in the original bifurcating autoregressive mode by allowing larger correlations between cousin cells and other cells in the same generation Huggins Basawa only considered maximum likelihood inference based on independent trees This paper examines the asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimators based on a single large tree

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents an innovative approach to statistical inference for the extended bifurcating autoregressive model specifically tailored to analyze cell lineage data Cell lineage studies are critical for understanding developmental biology and disease progression where the tracking of individual cell histories is essential The traditional modeling frameworks often fall short in capturing the complex branching structures inherent in lineage data We extend the bifurcating autoregressive model to incorporate additional parameters that allow for the nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies observed in cell lineages Using a combination of simulation studies and realcase biological datasets we carefully evaluate the performance of our model in terms of parameter estimation prediction accuracy and model robustness We employ Bayesian inference techniques to derive posterior distributions of the model parameters and provide a thorough discussion on the implications of our findings in the context of lineage tracing experiments The proposed model not only enhances the statistical understanding of cell dynamics but also offers a robust tool for researchers in developmental biology and medical research Our results demonstrate that the extended bifurcating autoregressive model significantly outperforms conventional methods paving the way for more nuanced interpretations of cell lineage data

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper presents a comprehensive statistical framework for the maximum likelihood estimation MLE of fractionally differenced autoregressive FAR models applied to twodimensional lattice data In recent years the increasing complexity of spatial data has underscored the importance of models that can adequately capture longrange dependencies and nonstationarity typically found in such datasets We explore the theoretical underpinnings of the FAR model in a twodimensional context demonstrating the implications of fractional differencing on both spectral properties and spatial correlation structure By employing a latticebased approach we derive the likelihood function for the FAR process taking into account the spatial interactions among neighboring lattice points We propose computationally efficient algorithms for estimating the model parameters including the fractional differencing parameter autoregressive coefficients and noise variance We rigorously validate our methods through extensive simulations showing robustness and accuracy in parameter recovery across varying lattice configurations and fractional orders Furthermore the methodology is applied to realworld spatial data illustrating the models efficacy in capturing complex phenomena where conventional stationary processes fall short Our findings contribute to the growing literature on spatial time series modeling and provide practitioners with a powerful tool for analyzing spatial dynamics in various fields including environmental studies finance and epidemiology

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper introduces a novel class of firstorder observationdriven integervalued autoregressive processes INAR which extend traditional autoregressive frameworks by incorporating stochastic dependence structures suitable for count data We establish the theoretical foundations of our model demonstrating its capacity to capture overdispersion and autocorrelation commonly observed in count time series The model employs a flexible linking function that facilitates the connection between the latent processes and observed counts allowing for a rich representation of the underlying datagenerating mechanisms We provide a thorough statistical estimation procedure utilizing the method of moments alongside an expectationmaximization EM algorithm for parameter estimation Additionally we conduct extensive simulation studies to evaluate the performance of the proposed model in recovering true parameter values under various scenarios Realworld applications are presented illustrating the models efficacy in capturing the dynamics of count data such as daily incidence of infectious diseases and retail sales transactions Our findings suggest that the firstorder observationdriven INAR processes are a powerful tool for modeling integervalued time series offering insights into both theoretical and practical aspects of count data analysis

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Limit distributions of prediction errors when the parameters are estimated are obtained for a general class of nonstationary processes that includes supercritical branching processes and explosive autoregressive processes as typical examples The estimated prediction errors are used to construct new tests of fit whose limit distributions are also derived

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic distributions of prediction errors for nonstationary processes providing a comprehensive framework for understanding the behavior of these errors as the sample size tends to infinity We derive the limiting distributions of various prediction error metrics including mean squared prediction error and absolute prediction error under a range of conditions commonly encountered in realworld time series analysis Additionally we propose a suite of tests for assessing the goodnessoffit of forecasting models in the context of nonstationarity including modifications to established statistical tests that account for the unique characteristics of nonstationary data Through extensive simulations we discuss the practical implications of our findings illustrating how the asymptotic results can inform model selection and evaluation in nonstationary settings Our results extend the existing literature by providing a rigorous statistical foundation for prediction accuracy assessment in nonstationary frameworks with applications across various fields including economics finance and environmental science By highlighting the significance of asymptotic behavior in prediction errors this study aims to enhance the reliability of predictive modeling in the presence of nonstationarity

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: A twodimensional time series model with longmemory dependence is introduced The model is based on a fractionally differenced autoregressive process longmemory combined with a standard pth order stationary autoregressive process shortmemory The maximum likelihood estimators for the parameters in the model are derived and their asymptotic distributions are obtained A novel feature of the derivations is that a new twodimensional martingale representation is used

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract Branching processes serve as fundamental models in various fields including biology epidemiology and finance for understanding growth dynamics and the spread of values over time This paper presents a suite of efficient statistical tests designed to assess and infer characteristics of branching processes We develop a framework that combines likelihoodbased methodologies with novel resampling techniques to enhance the robustness and power of hypothesis testing Specifically we introduce tests for key parameters such as reproduction ratios and extinction probabilities and evaluate their performance using simulation studies Our proposed tests exhibit improved efficiency in detecting deviations from null hypotheses when compared to existing methods particularly in smallsample scenarios We demonstrate the applicability of our tests through realworld data analysis showcasing their potential to provide insights into phenomena modeled by branching processes The findings contribute to the existing literature by offering practitioners in diverse fields a reliable set of tools for the statistical analysis of branching processes thereby advancing the understanding of complex systems governed by stochastic growth patterns

text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a novel approach to periodic time series modeling that emphasizes parsimony while maintaining robust predictive performance Traditional periodic time series models often struggle with overfitting due to the inclusion of excessive parameters leading to challenges in interpretability and generalization Our proposed method adopts a hierarchical framework that combines essential periodic components with a reduced number of parameters enabling efficient modeling of seasonal patterns without sacrificing accuracy By leveraging recent advancements in regularization techniques and Bayesian inference we demonstrate how our approach can effectively capture complex cyclical behaviors in various datasets We provide empirical evidence through extensive simulations and realworld applications highlighting the benefits of simplicity and interpretability without compromising on forecasting capability The findings suggest that our parsimonious model not only streamlines the modeling process but also enhances understanding of underlying seasonal dynamics making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners working with periodic time series data

text: The paper is concerned with the problem of estimating predicting unobserved counts based on partially observed multinomial panel data from several independent realizations of finite Markov chains The minimum meansquared error predictors depend on unknown model parameters which need to be estimated from the same data The maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters and their limit distributions are derived The decomposition and approximations of the prediction meansquared error of the estimated predictors are discussed

text: Models for timedependent contingency tables are presented Multinomiallogit conditional exponential family Markov chain and multinomialDirichlet models are discussed for bivariate binary time series The models are applied to two real data sets c Elsevier BV

text: In a previous paper Basawa efficient conditional tests were discussed for mixture experiments involving dependent observations The present paper is devoted to a study of the performance in large samples of a conditional maximum likelihood estimator and of a confidence limit for a parameter in a model specified by a mixture of a twoparameter exponential family The conditional estimator proposed in the paper is free from the mixing distribution and is efficient for all reasonable mixing distributions

text: Finite mixtures of Markov processes with densities belonging to exponential families are introduced Quasilikelihood and maximum likelihood methods are used to estimate the parameters of the mixing distributions and of the component distributions The EM algorithm is used to compute the ML estimates Mixture of Autoregressive processes and of twostate Markov chains are discussed as specific examples Simulation results on the comparison of quasilikelihood and ML estimates are reported C Elsevier Science BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Exact and asymptotic distributions of the maximum likelihood estimator of the autoregressive parameter in a firstorder bifurcating autoregressive process with exponential innovations are derived The limit distributions for the stationary critical and explosive cases are unified via a single pivot using a random normalization The pivot is shown to be asymptotically exponential for all values of the autoregressive parameter

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: This article is concerned with explosive AR processes generated by conditionally heteroscedastic errors Conditional least squares as well as generalized least squares estimation for autoregressive parameter are discussed and relevant limiting distributions are expressed as products of certain random variables These results can be viewed as generalizations of classical results obtained for the standard explosive ARl model with iid errors cf Fuller WA Introduction to Statistical Time Series second ed Wiley New York Chapter The model under consideration accommodates diverse conditionally heteroscedastic processes including Engle Autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity with estimates of the variance of UK inflation Econometrica s ARCH thresholdARCH and betaARCH processes Based on residuals least squares estimation for parameters appearing in the conditional variance is also discussed and is illustrated for various ARCH type processes C Elsevier BV

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractThis paper explores the properties of nonlinear time series models that are contiguous to firstorder autoregressive AR processes By establishing a theoretical framework we analyze the asymptotic behavior of nonlinear models that exhibit characteristics similar to AR processes under certain conditions Our study focuses on the identification of specific nonlinear transformations and their implications for time series data including patterns of autocorrelation and spectral behavior We introduce a novel efficiency test designed to assess the linearity of time series data in the presence of nonlinearities This test is grounded in a robust statistical methodology that accounts for potential misspecification commonly encountered in empirical analyses Through simulation studies and realdata applications we demonstrate the superior performance of our test in distinguishing between linear and nonlinear processes even in the presence of noise and structural breaks Our findings contribute to the literature on time series analysis by providing a methodological advancement for testing linearity and by enhancing the understanding of the connections between nonlinear dynamics and AR processes The implications of our results are significant for both theoretical research and practical applications in econometrics finance and other fields that utilize time series data
