author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the maximum likelihood estimation MLE for a firstorder bifurcating autoregressive process characterized by exponential error distributions Bifurcating autoregressive models are increasingly recognized for their ability to capture dynamic systems exhibiting branching behavior particularly in ecological and financial contexts We derive the likelihood function for the proposed model and demonstrate its properties under different parameter configurations Through a comprehensive simulation study we evaluate the performance of MLE in terms of bias efficiency and consistency alongside comparison with traditional autoregressive methods Our results indicate that the MLE approach provides robust parameter estimates in the presence of exponential error noise highlighting the advantages of modeling branching dynamics with appropriate error structures Additionally we present a realworld application to illustrate the practical implications of our findings This work contributes to the statistical toolbox for analyzing bifurcating processes and offers guidance for researchers dealing with complex time series data that exhibit nonlinear patterns and branching behavior

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the efficiency of conditional maximumlikelihood estimators CMLEs for parameter estimation in the context of mixtures of exponential families Mixtures of exponential families are widely used in statistical modeling due to their flexibility in accommodating diverse data distributions We derive the asymptotic properties of the CMLEs including their bias and variance and assess their efficiency relative to other estimation methods Additionally we propose confidence limits based on the CMLEs and evaluate their performance using simulation studies Our findings illustrate that CMLEs achieve asymptotic normality and exhibit a significant reduction in variance compared to traditional maximumlikelihood estimators in certain mixture settings The proposed confidence limits demonstrate good coverage properties across various sample sizes and mixture configurations enhancing inferential capabilities This study contributes to the understanding of parameter estimation in complex models and provides practical guidance for applying CMLEs in realworld scenarios involving mixtures of exponential families

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the application of categorical time series models to analyze contingency tables which are pivotal in many fields such as social sciences epidemiology and market research Traditional analysis of contingency tables often relies on crosssectional methods potentially overlooking the temporal dynamics inherent in categorical data We propose a framework that integrates time series techniques with categorical data analysis allowing for the investigation of temporal dependencies and trends within contingency tables Our approach incorporates innovations in marginal modeling and hierarchical structures to effectively capture the complexity of categorical time series We illustrate the methodology through simulations and realworld case studies highlighting the advantages of our models in identifying significant patterns over time Additionally we discuss model selection criteria and diagnostics for assessing model fit The findings underscore the importance of considering temporal aspects in categorical data analysis providing a robust tool for researchers seeking to unravel the dynamics of categorical responses across time

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: AbstractIn many realworld applications data are often only partially observed leading to challenges in accurately estimating true population parameters This paper presents a framework for estimating unobserved counts from partially observed multinomial distributions focusing on scenarios where only a subset of categories is visible due to sampling constraints or data collection limitations We employ a Bayesian approach to model the incomplete data structure incorporating prior information to enhance estimation accuracy The proposed method utilizes a Markov Chain Monte Carlo MCMC algorithm to sample from the posterior distribution of the unobserved counts allowing for uncertainty quantification in the estimates We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through simulations and realworld case studies highlighting its robustness in recovering unobserved counts under varying degrees of missingness Our findings suggest that the Bayesian framework not only improves estimation precision but also provides a systematic way to account for uncertainty in the unobserved categories This work contributes to the broader field of statistical inference under missing data mechanisms offering practical tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with incomplete multinomial data

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive framework for nonparametric estimation of nondecreasing Lvy processes a class of stochastic processes characterized by their continuous and nondecreasing paths We introduce a kernelbased estimation approach to recover the distribution of increments and the characteristics of the Lvy measure without imposing parametric assumptions Our methodology leverages the unique structure of nondecreasing Lvy processes allowing for consistent estimation of both the drift and the jump components We derive asymptotic results that establish the consistency and convergence rates of the proposed estimators supported by finitesample simulations that illustrate their effectiveness Additionally we apply our method to realworld data showcasing its practical utility in financial modeling and risk assessment This work expands the toolkit available for researchers and practitioners dealing with nondecreasing Lvy processes facilitating better inference and understanding of complex stochastic dynamics in various applications

text: AbstractThis paper explores the application of Generalized Least Squares GLS estimation in the context of explosive autoregressive processes of order one AR with conditionally heteroscedastic errors While explosive AR models are crucial in various fields such as finance and environmental science their estimation poses significant challenges due to nonstationarity and the presence of timevarying volatility We develop a robust framework for GLS estimation that accounts for the explosive behavior in time series data and the heteroscedasticity of the error terms Our approach incorporates a flexible specification of the variance structure allowing for the modeling of dynamic volatility patterns commonly observed in practice We derive the theoretical properties of the proposed estimator including consistency and asymptotic normality under suitable assumptions Additionally we provide simulation studies to illustrate the performance of the GLS estimator compared to traditional methods highlighting its advantages in terms of bias reduction and efficiency in finite samples Application of the methodology to empirical datasets demonstrates its effectiveness in capturing volatile behaviors inherent in explosive processes Overall our findings contribute to the statistical literature by offering a novel estimation technique applicable to a range of economic and financial time series characterized by explosive and heteroscedastic dynamics

author: Ishwar Basawa
text: Three nonparametric estimates of the measure corresponding to a nondecreasing Levy process are discussed Consistency and the limit distributions of the estimates are studied The empirical process corresponding to one of the estimates is briefly discussed with an anticipation of an application to goodnessoffit tests
